title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with mixed fortunes this week, from funding rounds to critical design reviews. Meanwhile, the Space Force grapples with cost concerns and launch risks, while international players continue to assert their presence.

themes.title: Funding Flows and Risks
themes.body: Chinese satellite manufacturer Hongqing's $191 million raise highlights the ongoing investment interest in space, even as the GAO flags cost concerns in the Space Force's portfolio. This juxtaposition underscores the precarious balance between innovation and fiscal responsibility.

themes.title: Launch Activity Picks Up
themes.body: Pegasus's Swift reboost mission and Isar Aerospace's contract for a Planet imaging satellite signal a steady pulse in launch activity. However, the persistent delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests remind us that not all launches are created equal.

themes.title: Defense Tech's New Frontiers
themes.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program and Anduril's collaboration with L3Harris on a tactical SDA constellation bid reflect a growing trend of defense tech integration in space. As the lines blur, expect more 'AI for Defense' startups to emerge from the woodwork.

themes.title: International Dynamics Emerge
themes.body: Russia's co-orbital activities near commercial GEO slots and GPS jamming returning to pre-2024 levels signal rising tensions in space. Meanwhile, allied workshops, like the one in The Hague, aim to bolster resilience against these emerging threats.
